judged_text: In sharing mode the Response handed to handleLarkError comes from the generic sync endpoint, whose documented contract is 'only the access token and expiry date', not Lark's {code, msg, data} envelope. The parsed body has no code field, so handleLarkError classifies every sync response as an API error and throws; Lark Calendar token refresh can never succeed under credential sharing.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, token refresh now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "lark-calendar", credential.userId)` and then unconditionally passes the returned `resp` into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) explicitly documents that in sharing mode it calls the generic `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and that "The response should only contain the access token and expiry date". That response will not be the Lark refresh endpoint’s expected shape, so routing it through `handleLarkError` (which is designed for Lark API responses) is incompatible and can break refresh under sharing mode.
